meta.title: Sanborn: proposed Rust harness with Laya

cards.title: Fast path: fewer reasoning turns
items: Execute explicit ready steps locally; do not invent new actions.
Bound read concurrency. Check dependencies before batching.
Cache only valid results; invalidate affected reads after edits and conservatively after shell execution.

cards.title: Control and trust
items: Laya never grants permissions, invents edits, or certifies success.
Continuation advice is usable only with satisfied plan preconditions.
Invalid plans, tool failures and uncertain decisions return to reasoning.
Acceptance evidence and a final response are required; an exhausted plan is not proof of success.

cards.title: Optional decision backend
items: Laya is a contract, not a confirmed installed model.
Use a verified local or approved hosted decision backend; no credentials in diagram artifacts.
Missing backend, timeout, malformed answer or low confidence produces explicit Absent and a recorded reason.
Run decisions in shadow mode first; calibrate thresholds on labeled synthetic fixtures.

cards.title: Proposed architecture, not implemented wiring
items: Existing core has a model/tool loop with parallel read batches and serialized mutations.
Bounded plans, decision routing, invalidation-aware caching and inference integrations are proposed additions.
Local event traces record durations, decisions, fallbacks, tokens and acceptance outcomes; redact sensitive payloads.
Compare baseline, deterministic plans and plans plus Laya with identical reasoning backends and tasks.
Select for time to a correct result and success rate, not merely fewer turns.
